teams.note: Hakan Calhanoglu is one of the cleaner calls in the whole tournament file. Transfermarkt's Turkiye national-team penalty log shows him converting against Bulgaria in World Cup qualifying in November 2025 and against Germany in the March 2025 Nations League play-off, which is exactly the kind of repeated recent senior evidence that moves a side into the high-confidence bucket. Arda Guler is the best secondary name to carry because he is Turkiye's other elite technical attacker and the most believable alternative if Calhanoglu is absent or cedes the duty.
evidence_log: 15 Nov 2025: Transfermarkt's Turkiye national-team penalty log records Hakan Calhanoglu converting in the 2-0 World Cup qualifying win over Bulgaria.
23 Mar 2025: the same national-team log also records Calhanoglu converting Turkiye's penalty against Germany in the Nations League play-off.
Current working view: two recent senior penalties from the same taker make Calhanoglu a strong high-confidence World Cup call, with Arda Guler the clearest technical fallback.

teams.last_evidence: 3 Jun 2026 audit: Balogun club penalty profile and World Cup striker-role evidence now outrank Tillman as the market-facing USA backup behind Pulisic.
teams.note: Christian Pulisic remains the USA primary when he is on the pitch. The secondary has been moved from Malik Tillman to Folarin Balogun. Tillman did take the USA in-match penalty in the 2025 Gold Cup quarter-final when Pulisic and several A-team attackers were absent, but that kick was missed and came in an alternate-squad context. Balogun has the stronger penalty-taker profile: he is a centre-forward, is in the final World Cup striker group, entered camp in strong scoring form for Monaco and the USA, and has a much deeper senior club penalty record. Market-facing hierarchy: Pulisic first; Balogun second if Pulisic is absent or defers; Tillman remains a live tertiary/alternate-squad option rather than the best full-strength backup.
evidence_log: 9 Sep 2023: U.S. Soccer and SofaScore both show Christian Pulisic converted the late in-match penalty in the 3-0 win over Uzbekistan.
6 Jun 2021: U.S. Soccer shows Pulisic scored the decisive extra-time penalty against Mexico in a major senior final.
31 May 2026: U.S. Soccer named Balogun among the three final-roster World Cup strikers and described his strong 2025-26 scoring form for Monaco and the USMNT.

3 Jun 2026 audit: Transfermarkt lists Balogun with a substantially deeper penalty record than Tillman, including 2025-26 Monaco penalties, which makes him the stronger specialist backup behind Pulisic.

29 Jun 2025: U.S. Soccer shows Tillman took and missed the USA in-match penalty against Costa Rica in the Gold Cup quarter-final; useful alternate-squad evidence, but not enough to keep him above Balogun in a full-strength World Cup hierarchy.
Current working view: Pulisic remains clear primary; Balogun is now the market-facing secondary; Tillman is tertiary/alternate-squad context.

teams.last_evidence: 2 Jun 2026 injury audit: De Arrascaeta became a World Cup doubt after a calf/muscle issue in Uruguay training; Bentancur was Uruguay's No. 2 shooter in both 2024 Copa America shootouts behind Valverde.
teams.note: Federico Valverde remains the clear Uruguay primary. The March 2026 Wembley penalty is the freshest in-match evidence, and the 2024 Copa America shootout order already placed him first. The backup line now moves from Giorgian De Arrascaeta to Rodrigo Bentancur. This is not because De Arrascaeta has lost status when fully fit; it is because he is now an active World Cup injury doubt after leaving Uruguay training with a calf/muscle problem on 2 June. Bentancur is the safest in-squad secondary among regular starters because Uruguay trusted him immediately after Valverde in both major 2024 Copa America shootouts, and he converted both. If De Arrascaeta is passed fully fit and starts, he remains live in the hierarchy, but the market-facing backup should now be Bentancur until the medical picture clears.
evidence_log: 27 Mar 2026: ESPN and SofaScore both show Federico Valverde scored Uruguay's 90+4 minute penalty in the 1-1 friendly draw with England at Wembley.
2024 Copa America quarter-final vs Brazil: Uruguay's shootout order opened Valverde then Bentancur; both scored, with De Arrascaeta third.
2024 Copa America third-place match vs Canada: Uruguay again opened Valverde then Bentancur; both scored, with De Arrascaeta third and Suarez fourth.
2 Jun 2026: GE and La Diaria report De Arrascaeta suffered a calf/muscle issue in Uruguay training and will undergo tests, making his World Cup availability uncertain.
Current working view: Valverde remains high-confidence primary. Bentancur is promoted to secondary while De Arrascaeta is an injury doubt; De Arrascaeta remains live only if cleared and starting.
teams.squad_note: Coach: Marcelo Bielsa. Uruguay announced a 26-man World Cup squad with Federico Valverde, Rodrigo Bentancur and Giorgian De Arrascaeta included, but De Arrascaeta is an injury doubt after the 2 June training issue. Group H: Spain, Saudi Arabia, Uruguay, Cabo Verde.

teams.last_evidence: Olympics 2024, WCQ 2025 and later shootout order
teams.note: Eldor Shomurodov should now be treated as a high-confidence Uzbekistan primary. The pattern is very consistent: captain, all-time leading scorer, penalty taker in historic moments, and still trusted after misses. He scored Uzbekistan's first-ever Olympic goal from the spot against Spain, then later took and missed the World Cup qualifying penalty against Kyrgyz Republic without losing status, and still led the later shootout order. Otabek Shukurov remains the best named secondary because he is the only other direct recent Uzbekistan taker in the file, but this page should be centred clearly around Shomurodov.
evidence_log: 24 Jul 2024: Shomurodov scored Uzbekistan's first-ever Olympic goal from the penalty spot against Spain.
20 Mar 2025: Championat.asia's World Cup qualifying report states Eldor Shomurodov took Uzbekistan's in-match penalty against Kyrgyz Republic and the goalkeeper saved it.
5 Sep 2025: Championat.asia's CAFA coverage shows Otabek Shukurov later converted a penalty for Uzbekistan against Kyrgyz Republic.
18 Nov 2025: SofaScore's shootout order against Iran shows Shomurodov still taking the first Uzbekistan penalty in the tiebreak.
Current working view: Shomurodov is a high-confidence Uzbekistan primary, with Shukurov the clearest named fallback rather than a true rival for the lead role.
